nodes.label: DOWNLOAD_REFS
nodes.notes: Runs once. Fetches genome FASTA, GTF and cDNA FASTA for one Ensembl species and release, writes download_log.txt and reference_metadata.json.

nodes.label: references/ (v<release>/ when pinned)
nodes.notes: Published: *.dna.*.fa.gz, *.gtf.gz, *.cdna.all.fa.gz, download_log.txt, reference_metadata.json. Nothing in DOWNLOAD consumes them; they are inputs to a later BUILD_INDICES or RNASEQ run.

nodes.label: DOWNLOAD_GMT
nodes.notes: Runs once, only with --download_gmt. Needs network at run time: msigdbr fetches gene sets on first use.

nodes.label: gmt/
nodes.notes: hallmark.gmt, c2_curated.gmt, c2_kegg.gmt, c2_reactome.gmt, c5_go.gmt, c5_go_bp.gmt

nodes.label: STAR_GENOME_GENERATE
nodes.notes: Runs once. --sjdbGTFfile from the GTF; --genomeSAindexNbases derived from genome size.

nodes.label: HISAT2_BUILD
nodes.notes: Runs once. Splice-aware when memory allows; drops --ss/--exon and warns otherwise (see USAGE, HISAT2 index memory).

nodes.label: SALMON_INDEX
nodes.notes: Runs once. Decoy-aware: the genome is the decoy set.

nodes.label: KALLISTO_INDEX
nodes.notes: Runs once. Transcripts only, no decoys.

nodes.label: map { row -> [meta, [reads]] }
nodes.notes: Builds meta from the row: id = sample, condition = condition, single_end = (R2 empty). Extra columns such as batch are NOT carried into meta; the DE scripts re-read the samplesheet for them.

nodes.label: map { name, reads -> [meta, reads] }
nodes.notes: meta.id = the pair name; single_end from the list length. No condition, so nothing downstream of counts can contrast anything.

nodes.label: ch_reads
nodes.notes: The workflow's single take:. Shape is identical on both input routes; meta differs by one key.

nodes.label: FASTQC
nodes.notes: One task per sample, on the raw reads.

nodes.label: FASTP
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Every aligner consumes FASTP.out.reads, never the raw reads.

nodes.label: FASTP.out.reads
nodes.notes: Not a named workflow variable: consumed directly as FASTP.out.reads by whichever aligner runs.

nodes.label: STAR_ALIGN
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Takes the GTF as --sjdbGTFfile, so --gtf is a hard requirement on this route, unguarded at rnaseq.nf:460 (to-fix M21).

nodes.label: star/
nodes.notes: BAMs, .bai (from SAMTOOLS_INDEX), Log.final.out, Log.out, Log.progress.out, ReadsPerGene.out.tab

nodes.label: ch_bams
nodes.notes: Initialised channel.empty() at 444 and reassigned by whichever genome aligner ran. The empty initialiser is a dangling source node in every preview DAG.

nodes.label: HISAT2_ALIGN
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Takes no GTF: splice sites are baked into the index at build time.

nodes.label: SALMON_QUANT
nodes.notes: One task per sample. --libType A: infers strandedness itself, so RSeQC is not needed and not run.

nodes.label: KALLISTO_QUANT
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Cannot infer strandedness; with --strandedness auto it runs library-type-agnostic and a notice is recorded.

nodes.label: results.collect { row -> row[1] }
nodes.notes: Drops meta. Downstream R scripts re-derive sample identity from the directory names, which are meta.id, and from the samplesheet.

nodes.label: SAMTOOLS_INDEX
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Passes the BAM through beside the new .bai.

nodes.label: ch_bam_bai
nodes.notes: The genome-route spine: RSeQC, BigWig and rMATS all read this. Initialised channel.empty() at 520.

nodes.label: GTF2BED
nodes.notes: Runs once. BED12 for RSeQC. Not published.

nodes.label: RSEQC
nodes.notes: One task per sample. infer_experiment, read_distribution, geneBody_coverage, and a one-word strandedness verdict per sample.

nodes.label: BAM_TO_BIGWIG
nodes.notes: One task per sample. deepTools bamCoverage, CPM-normalised.

nodes.label: STAR_FUSION
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Never previewed: no yeast CTAT library exists. Wiring transcribed from rnaseq.nf:467-474.

nodes.label: map { meta, bam, bai -> [meta.id, bam, bai, meta.single_end] }

operator.closure: map { meta, bam, bai -> [meta.id, bam, bai, meta.single_end] }

nodes.notes: C3 lived here. This map used to emit [bam, bai] and drop meta.id, forcing run_rmats.py to match BAMs to samples by filename substring: ctrl1 claimed ctrl10.bam. Fixed 2026-09-01 by carrying the id.

nodes.label: collect(flat: false)
nodes.notes: flat: false keeps each [id, bam, bai, single_end] as a sub-list. The order of the list is the order run_rmats.py pairs ids to BAMs; both come from this one closure, so it is exact.

nodes.label: map { rows -> [ [id:'all_samples', single_end, ids], bams, bais ] }

operator.closure: map { rows -> [ [id:'all_samples', single_end, ids], bams, bais ] }

nodes.notes: Collapses N per-sample items into ONE cohort item. Errors if single_end differs across samples (H7): rMATS takes one -t for the cohort. This is where per-sample metadata becomes per-cohort.

nodes.label: RMATS
nodes.notes: Runs once for the cohort. run_rmats.py builds b1/b2 per contrast from the samplesheet, REF last (M19). --gtf is unguarded at rnaseq.nf:571 (to-fix M21): a HISAT2 run without a GTF dies here.

nodes.label: rmats_output/<condition>_vs_REF/
nodes.notes: Ten MATS files per contrast plus rMATS intermediates (fromGTF.*, *.raw.input.*, tmp/, b1.txt, b2.txt).

nodes.label: ch_quarto_rmats
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) by default; reassigned to RMATS.out.results when rMATS ran. The ninth QUARTO_REPORT input, added 2026-09-02.

nodes.label: RSEQC.out.strandedness.map { meta, txt -> [meta, txt.text.trim()] }
nodes.notes: Reads the file's one word into a val at workflow-construction time.

nodes.label: ch_bams.map { meta, _bam -> [meta, params.strandedness] }
nodes.notes: Every sample gets the same user-supplied value. No RSeQC verdict is consulted, so a wrong --strandedness silently halves counts.

nodes.label: ch_bams.join(ch_strand)
nodes.notes: Joins on meta as the key: both sides carry the identical meta map, which is what makes the join exact. If either side's meta gained or lost a key, every sample would silently fail to pair.

nodes.label: map { meta, bam, strand -> [meta, bam, gtf_file, strand] }

operator.closure: map { meta, bam, strand -> [meta, bam, gtf_file, strand] }

nodes.notes: Folds the GTF path into every item rather than passing it as a separate value input.

nodes.label: FEATURECOUNTS
nodes.notes: One task per sample. Runs at level 2 (postQC), not level 3 as the docs say (to-fix M22). -p for paired; subread 2.0.1 semantics (M20).

nodes.label: counts.collect { row -> row[1] }
nodes.notes: Drops meta. DESeq2 and edgeR re-derive sample identity from the count-file names, which are <sample>.featureCounts.txt, and from the samplesheet.

nodes.label: FEATURECOUNTS_EXON
nodes.notes: One task per sample. featureCounts -f -O: exon-level, for the exon-usage diffSplice test. Same input channel as FEATURECOUNTS.

nodes.label: GTF2GENEINFO
nodes.notes: Runs once. gene_id, gene_name, gene_biotype from the GTF. Not published; annotates every DE table.

nodes.label: ch_gene_info
nodes.notes: channel.empty() unless the GTF is present. DESeq2 and edgeR take it as a path input, so an empty channel here starves them (M4).

nodes.label: TXIMPORT
nodes.notes: Runs once. Summarises transcript quantification to gene level; dropInfReps = TRUE (1.5.1). The txi object carries counts, abundance and lengths for length-aware DE.

nodes.label: ch_de_counts
nodes.notes: Three sources, one per route. Shape differs: a list of per-sample count tables (genome aligners), one txi.rds (pseudo-aligners), or one matrix file (--counts). deseq2.R and edger.R detect which they were given. Starved when genome aligner with no --gtf: ch_featurecounts_results is channel.empty(), DESEQ2 and EDGER are wired and never run (M4).

nodes.label: DESEQ2
nodes.notes: Runs once for all contrasts. Baseline from RNASEQ_FLOW_REFERENCE_LEVEL (env, from --reference_level). Every contrast is <condition>_vs_<baseline>. Starved when a genome aligner without --gtf: input channel empty, process never executes, no error (M4).

nodes.label: deseq2_output/
nodes.notes: Result CSVs per contrast, figures as SVG and PNG, reproduce/

nodes.label: ch_quarto_deseq2
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) by default; reassigned to the results dir when the stage ran.

nodes.label: EDGER
nodes.notes: Runs once for all contrasts. Baseline from RNASEQ_FLOW_REFERENCE_LEVEL (env, from --reference_level). Every contrast is <condition>_vs_<baseline>. Starved when a genome aligner without --gtf: input channel empty, process never executes, no error (M4).

nodes.label: edger_output/
nodes.notes: Result CSVs per contrast, figures as SVG and PNG, reproduce/

nodes.label: ch_quarto_edger
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) by default; reassigned to the results dir when the stage ran.

nodes.label: DTU
nodes.notes: Runs once. DEXSeq on dtuScaledTPM. Opt-in; compute-heavy.

nodes.label: DIFFSPLICE (exon)
nodes.notes: The same process, invoked with level='exon'. Runs once. edgeR diffSpliceDGE. One invocation per run, never both: the route decides which.

nodes.label: DIFFSPLICE (transcript)
nodes.notes: The same process, invoked with level='transcript'. Runs once. edgeR diffSpliceDGE. One invocation per run, never both: the route decides which.

nodes.label: diffsplice_output/
nodes.notes: Not staged into the report.

nodes.label: ISOFORM_SWITCH
nodes.notes: Runs once. Salmon only. --gtf unguarded at rnaseq.nf:495 (to-fix M21). Figures written by the package itself, so outside the reproduce/ conventions (M17).

nodes.label: results.collect { row -> row[1] }
nodes.notes: A second, separate collect of SALMON_QUANT.out.results; ch_tx_quant is not reused.

nodes.label: GSEA
nodes.notes: Runs once. fgsea on the DESeq2 ranked list per contrast. Needs --gmt.

nodes.label: ch_quarto_gsea
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) unless GSEA ran.

nodes.label: GPROFILER
nodes.notes: Runs once. Over-representation of the DESeq2 up and down lists. Needs network for g:Profiler's API.

nodes.label: ch_quarto_gprofiler
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) unless gProfiler ran.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files
nodes.notes: channel.empty() at 454, grown by eight mix calls. Every contributor is a collect { row -> row[1] } that drops meta: MultiQC identifies samples from filenames, which is why sample-name reconciliation (--replace-names) exists.

nodes.label: ch_align_results
nodes.notes: STAR Log.final.out, HISAT2 summary, or the Salmon/Kallisto results dirs, collected. Whichever aligner ran.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files.mix(...)
nodes.notes: Unconditional. Mixes channel.empty() when the contributing stage did not run.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files.mix(...)
nodes.notes: Unconditional. Mixes channel.empty() when the contributing stage did not run.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files.mix(...)
nodes.notes: Unconditional. Mixes channel.empty() when the contributing stage did not run.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files.mix(...)
nodes.notes: Unconditional. Mixes channel.empty() when the contributing stage did not run.

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_files.collect()
nodes.notes: The collect that makes MULTIQC run ONCE over everything rather than once per file.

nodes.label: MULTIQC
nodes.notes: Runs once. Skipped entirely for a --counts run. Also converts software_versions.yml into the software_versions_mqc.yml custom-content section.

nodes.label: multiqc/
nodes.notes: rnaseq-flow_multiqc_report.html and rnaseq-flow_multiqc_report_data/

nodes.label: ch_multiqc_data
nodes.notes: channel.value([]) for a --counts run; MULTIQC.out.data otherwise. Staged under its incoming name, rnaseq-flow_multiqc_report_data, so the report can derive the report filename from it.

nodes.label: ch_versions
nodes.notes: channel.empty() at 390, grown by one mix per process. Per-sample processes contribute .first() so one versions.yml per process, not per task.

nodes.label: collectFile(name: 'software_versions.yml')
nodes.notes: Concatenates every process's versions.yml into one file. Each module's heredoc has to survive stripIndent() for this to be valid YAML (check_report.py guards it).

nodes.label: channel.of(JSON of buildRunManifest(design, notices))
nodes.notes: Built at workflow-construction time, so it records configuration, not outcome.

nodes.label: collectFile(name: 'run_manifest.json', storeDir: tracedir)
nodes.notes: storeDir publishes it to pipeline_info/ as a side effect of staging it.

nodes.label: first()
nodes.notes: Makes it a value channel, matching the report's other inputs.

nodes.label: QUARTO_REPORT
nodes.notes: Always runs, once. Nine inputs: value channels and one-item queue channels only, which is what keeps it to a single task. Renders whichever sections have data.

nodes.label: ch_versions.mix(QUARTO_REPORT.out.versions)
nodes.notes: The workflow's single emit. Nothing consumes it: MULTIQC already ran before the report existed, so the report's own version never reaches software_versions.
